question:
int fd = open("file.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT, 0644);
Why is 0644 a permission mask?
options: 0644 is an octal literal representing file permissions (rw-r--r--); the leading 0 denotes octal
0644 is a decimal number
0644 is a hexadecimal color code
Compiler error: octal literals are not allowed
explanation: Octal 0644 = rw-r--r-- (owner read/write, group read, others read); 0 prefix signals octal parsing.

options: 42 (exit status extracted by WEXITSTATUS macro)
0 (wait always returns 0)
Compiler error: WEXITSTATUS is not standard
Garbage value
explanation: wait() obtains the child's exit status; WEXITSTATUS extracts the exit code passed to exit().

options: execv replaces the current process image; the old code (printf) is no longer in memory
execv returns control but suppresses output
printf is executed by the new process
Compiler error: execv is not standard C
explanation: execv() replaces the entire process; subsequent code only runs if execv fails.

options: Closes the read end to reduce file descriptor usage; the child only writes, not reads
Prevents the child from reading the pipe
Closes the entire pipe
Compiler error: cannot close pipe file descriptors
explanation: Pipes are bidirectional; each process closes unused ends to signal EOF when writing ends.

options: Signal handlers are asynchronous and may interrupt printf; unbuffered writes to stderr are safer; the handler cannot safely call many functions
Signals always run safely
raise() always delivers the signal immediately
Compiler error: signal handlers cannot call printf
explanation: Signal handlers have limited async-signal-safety; calling printf is risky (not in the whitelist).

The file creation time
The file permissions

explanation: stat() fills a struct with file metadata; st_size is the byte count of the file.

The process ID and parent process ID

To specify the number of directories to read
